templates.pattern: Eight persons [P1]-[P8] belong to different states and different professions. They are arranged in a row. States: UP,MP,MH,TN,KA,WB,RJ,GJ. Professions: IAS,IPS,IFS,IRS,IES,IRTS,IDAS,IRAS. [P1] is from UP and is IAS, sits at position [POS1] from left. [P4] is from MH and is IPS, sits at position [POS4]. [P6] is from TN and is IFS, sits between [P4] and [P8]. [P2] is from WB and sits at extreme left. [P8] is from KA and is IRS at extreme right. [P3] is from MP and is IES. [P7] is from RJ and is IRTS, sits to immediate left of [P8]. What position is [P5] from left?
templates.explanation: Row: [P2]-[P5]-[P1]-[P3]-[P4]-[P6]-[P7]-[P8]. [P5] is at position 2 from left

templates.pattern: Six friends [P1]-[P6] plan trips over 6 months (Jan-Jun). Each goes to a unique destination and uses a unique transport. Destinations: Paris, Tokyo, Dubai, NYC, Sydney, London. Transports: Flight, Ship, Train, Bus, Car, Bike. [P1] goes to Paris by Flight in Jan. [P3] goes in March by Ship. [P5] goes to Sydney by Car in May. [P2] goes to Dubai in Feb. [P4] goes to London in April. The person going to NYC uses Train. [P6] goes in June. [P4] uses Bus. Which transport does [P2] use?

Eight persons [P1]-[P8] have different amounts of money (Rs.): [M1],[M2],...[M8] in AP with common difference [D]. [P1] has Rs.[M1]. [P8] has the most. [P4] gives Rs.[G] to [P2]. After transaction: [P4] new amount - [P2] new amount = ?
templates.explanation: [P4]=M1+3D (4th in AP, index 3). [P2]=M1+D (2nd in AP). After: [P4]-G and [P2]+G. Diff=([P4]-G)-([P2]+G)=(M1+3D-G)-(M1+D+G)=2D-2G

templates.pattern: Nine students [P1]-[P9] wrote an exam with [Q] questions. Marks: +[R] for correct, -[W] for wrong, 0 for unattempted. [P1] attempted [A1] questions, got [C1] correct. [P3] attempted [A3], got [C3] correct. [P5] attempted all [Q] questions, got [C5] correct. Compare scores of [P1] and [P3]. Who scored more?

Seven persons [P1]-[P7] are assigned 7 consecutive room numbers [RN] to [RN+6] in a hotel. Each room has a different floor level (1-7). [P1] gets room [RN] on floor [FL]. [P3] gets room [RN+2] on a floor [K] above [P1]. [P5] gets a room [M] above [P3]'s room number, on floor [FL+K+1]. [P7] has the highest room number. What floor is [P5] on?

Ten persons [P1]-[P10] form 2 committees of 5 each. Committee 1: [P1],[P2],[P3],[P4],[P5]. Committee 2: [P6],[P7],[P8],[P9],[P10]. Each person has a unique skill rating 1-10. [P1]=[R1], [P3]=[R3], [P5]=[R5]. The average skill of Committee 1 = [AVG1]. [P7]=[R7], [P9]=[R9]. Average of Committee 2 = [AVG2]. What is the combined average of both committees?

Six persons [P1]-[P6] each have a different number of books (10,15,20,25,30,35). Each also has a different reading speed (pages/day): 20,25,30,35,40,45. [P1] has [B1] books of [PG] pages each and reads at [SP] pages/day. [P3] has twice as many books as [P1] but reads [K] pages/day faster. [P5] has the most books. Days for [P1] to finish all books = ?

Eight employees [P1]-[P8] work in a company. Their annual increments follow a rule: Increment = [BASE]% of current salary if performance > [THRESH], else [LOW]%. [P1] salary = Rs.[S]K, performance score = [PERF1]. [P3] salary = Rs.[S+5]K, performance score = [PERF3]. [P5] salary = Rs.[S+10]K, performance = [PERF5]. [THRESH] = [T]. What is [P1]'s salary after increment?
templates.explanation: [P1] performance [PERF1] > [T], so gets [BASE]% increment. New salary = S*(1+BASE/100) = [S]*(1+[BASE]/100)

templates.pattern: Six persons [P1]-[P6] sit in 2 rows facing each other (3 per row). Row 1 faces east. Row 2 faces west. Each person has a unique task and a unique completion time (hours). [P1] is in Row 1, task A, time [T1]hrs. [P4] faces [P1] in Row 2, task D, time [T4]hrs. [P3] is in Row 1 to the right of [P1], task C. [P6] faces [P3] in Row 2. [P2] is to the left of [P1] in Row 1. Total time for Row 1 = [TR1]. Total time for Row 2 = [TR2]. Difference in total times?

Nine persons [P1]-[P9] participated in a relay race in teams of 3. Team 1: [P1],[P2],[P3]. Team 2: [P4],[P5],[P6]. Team 3: [P7],[P8],[P9]. Each person ran a different distance (km): 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10. [P1] ran [D1]km, [P2] ran [D2]km, [P3] ran [D3]km. Team 1 total = [TT1]km. [P4] ran [D4]km, [P5] ran [D5]km. Team 2 total = [TT2]km. What did [P6] run?

Eight persons [P1]-[P8] are coded by numbers 1-8 in some arrangement. [P1]=code[C1], [P3]=code[C3], [P5]=code[C5]. The code follows: Person code = (floor position * [F]) + (row number * [R]) + [CONST]. [P2] is on floor [FL2], row [ROW2]. What is [P2]'s code?

Ten persons [P1]-[P10] attended a conference for [DAYS] days. Each attended a different number of sessions per day (1-10). [P1] attended [S1] sessions/day. Over [DAYS] days, [P1] total = [S1*DAYS]. [P3] attended [K] more sessions/day than [P1]. [P5] attended [M] fewer sessions/day than [P3]. Total sessions attended by [P1],[P3],[P5] combined over [DAYS] days?
